title: Gift guide picks
prompt: The gift guide shows products customers can still buy: home items under 60.00, and kitchen or outdoor items at 25.00 or less. Write `solve(products)` so it returns them as `product_id`, `product_name`, `category` and `price`.
rules: Only products whose `active` value is true appear.
Home products need a `unit_price` below 60.00. Kitchen and outdoor products need 25.00 or less. No other category appears.
A product with a missing price, category or `active` value is left out.
Return four columns in this order: `product_id`, `name` renamed to `product_name`, `category`, and `unit_price` renamed to `price` (still a decimal).
hints: Write the two price rules as two conditions, one for home and one for kitchen and outdoor, then join them with `|` inside one pair of parentheses.
`active` is already true or false, so `F.col("active")` can be used as a condition on its own. Join it to the price rules with `&`.
After `filter`, `select` the columns and rename two of them with `.alias(...)`, for example `F.col("name").alias("product_name")`.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(products):
    # Return product_id, product_name, category and price for the gift guide.
    return products
explanation: Build the two price rules separately: `home = (F.col("category") == "home") & (F.col("unit_price") < 60)` and `kit = F.col("category").isin("kitchen", "outdoor") & (F.col("unit_price") <= 25)`. A product needs either one, and it must be active: `products.filter(F.col("active") & (home | kit))`. The parentheses around `home | kit` matter: without them `&` is worked out first, and an inactive kitchen product slips back in. Then `select("product_id", F.col("name").alias("product_name"), "category", F.col("unit_price").alias("price"))` names the columns; `alias` changes only the name, so `price` stays a decimal. Missing values drop out by themselves, because a check on a missing value isn't true.
